premises.text: Open-source users face bugs and missing features with hard-to-get support while developers lack incentive or priority to fix them
premises.evidence_span: all this software has two properties in common, which is bugs and missing features

premises.text: Users can place paid incentives on issue pages with two clicks via integrations into major issue trackers
premises.evidence_span: allows you to pay or get paid directly from an issue page

premises.text: Multiple users can crowdfund one issue, and developers can request incentives or list issues for crowdfunding in one click
premises.evidence_span: many users can place incentives on one issue

premises.text: The service takes a 6% fee on successful incentives and shares fees with issue-system hosters
premises.evidence_span: we take a 6% fee for each successful incentive

premises.text: Distribution aim is panels on every bug/feature/support page, later extending beyond open source to app stores
premises.evidence_span: have our panel on every book page, every feature request, and in every support system

value.text: Users get paid support/fixes for software issues and developers get paid to improve them
value.evidence_span: place incentives for on demand software support

causal_links.evidence_span: mismatch in knowledge and priority between the user and the developer
with two clicks, a user can place an incentive
turns an issue system into a profit center
adding a monetization element to the entire open source market

notes: Bugs+missing features+hard support coded as one pain-bundle (P1). Named tracker integrations (Mantis/Jira/etc.) folded into P2. ASR 'book' for bug left in evidence spans verbatim. App-store next focus folded into P5 distribution vision as stated expansion of the same panel strategy. Singletons retained for pricing and distribution modules.
